Air Deccan, vs Ashwani Kumar Chugh on 25 January, 2008
IN THE STATE COMMISSION: DELHI

1
Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see
the Judgement.
2.     
To be referred to the Reporter or not.
Justice J.D. Kapoor (Oral)
1. On
account of rescheduling the flight inspite of having confirmed ticket for 7th
March, 2007, appellant Airlines has been vide impugned order dated 4th
October, 2007 been held guilty for deficiency in service and causing immense mental tension, harassment
and physical discomfort and inconvenience to the newly wedded couple, and has
thus been directed to pay compensation of Rs. 25,000/- along with cost of Rs.
2500/-. Feeling aggrieved the appellant has preferred this appeal.
2 Allegations
of the respondent leading to impugned order , in brief, were that respondent
was married in February, 2007 and planned to visit Goa for honeymoon during the period between
7.3.2007 to 12.3.2007. He also planned to visit Mumbai on 12/13.3.07 and return
to Delhi on 13.3.2007. He took ticket on-line to
travel by Air Deccan. When the respondent opened his e-mail, he noted that by mistake two
tickets had been allotted to him. He tried to cancel one ticket on internet but
failed and then managed to contract Customer Care number of the
appellant-airline and requested for cancellation of one ticket and refund of
the amount. Initially the functionary of the appellant informed the respondent
that Rs. 600/- to 700/- would be deducted for cancellation and when the respondent pointed out that allotment of
tickets for the same journey was due to negligence on the part of the appellant
that the appellant assured the respondent that he would be refunded the whole
amount. Appellant airline had issued confirmed ticket for journey of the
respondent and his wife from Delhi to Goa on 7.3.2007 and accordingly the
respondent reached the airport where to his shock there was no flight of the OP airline for Goa on 7.3.2007. The respondent requested the
official of the appellant to arrange shuffling flight from Delhi Mumbai and
then from Mumbai to Goa but his request was turned down. The
respondent then purchased ticket of Spicejet Airlines incurring an expenditure
of Rs. 8,096/- and reached Goa. On account of shortage of funds, as he was required to
spend extra money for purchase of tickets of Spicejet Airline, the respondent
had to curtail the tour. Instead of returning to Delhi on 13.3.2007 as planned, he returned to Delhi on 10.3.2007. He had to cancel his visit to Mumbai. On account of
deficiency on the part of the
appellant-airline, respondent and his wife not only faced physical inconvenience but suffered
great deal of mental agony as their honeymoon trip was spoiled. The respondent
besides seeking refund of the amount of tickets has sought compensation to the
tune of Rs. 3.5 lacs for mental and physical harassment. He has also sought directions to the appellant airline governing the operation
of the flights and customer care.
3. In
its defecne the plea taken by the appellant was that the respondent by mistake
had booked two tickets and though he was liable to be charged for cancellation
of the ticket, yet whole amount charged for that tickets was refunded. While admitting that it had issued tickets to the respondent for flight
from Delhi to Goa on 7.3.2007, the appellant airline averred that the departure
of the said flight was changed due to
some operational reasons and the said
flight was operational on 1,4,5,6, and 7th
day of the week in place of all days of
the week and, therefore, there was no flight scheduled for Goa on
7.3.2007 and the respondent was asked to reschedule his ticket but he declined
the offer.
4. The
aforesaid rival claims of the parties clearly make out a case of grossest kind
of deficiency in service. Admittedly the appellant airlines had issued the
tickets with confirmed status to the respondent for travel from Delhi to Goa on 7th March,
 2007. The ticket was obtained on internet about 5 days
back i.e. on 2-3rd March, 07. There is no doubt that two tickets were
allotted to the respondent and one was cancelled . It is also not in dispute
that refund of the cancellation was made to the respondent after about a months
time and that too after his repeated request.
5. It
is contended by the learned counsel for
the appellant that it was due to technical reasons which was beyond its control
when the flight was rescheduled under
intimation to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and further that the refund of the cancellation
of ticket was given to the respondent without deducting normal cancellation
charges and therefore appellant was
wrongly held guilty for deficiency in service.
6. In
view of the fact that respondent had obtained a ticket hardly 5 days before
scheduled flight and if at all there was rescheduling of the flight for 5 days a week, it could not have
taken place suddenly or
on spur of moment. Rescheduling of flight has to take place at the most
the day or two before and in that event it was statuary obligation of the appellant to
intimate the passenger travelling on the said flight individually. It was
natural for the respondent to get shocked on reaching the airport and come to know that there was no flight to Goa and, therefore,
he asked airline officials to accommodate him on any
other flight from Delhi to Goa but
that request was turned down. The respondent had already made the plans
and booked hotel in Goa for a particular day but every thing went haywire and having limited money
he had to spend out more than
8,000/- on the booking of other flight and the funds became short and as a result honeymoon trip
was shortened and thereby he suffered
mental agony, harassment, physical discomfort. He had to cancel his visit to
Mumbai and such a lapse on the part of
the appellant airlines who had taken the
issue so casually amounts to grossest kind of deficiency in
service as defined by
section 2(1)(d)
of the C.P. Act which means any fault,
imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of
performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time
being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance
of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service.
7. On the concept of
compensation to be awarded to a consumer in such circumstances the Hon'ble
Supreme Court in case after case and recently in
Ghaziabad
Development Authority Vs Balbir
Singh-
(2004) 5 Supreme court Cases 65 observed that every consumer has to be
compensated for each and every component of suffering, namely, mental agony,
harassment, physical discomfort, emotional suffering, insult, humiliation and other injustice and sufferings suffered
by the consumer at the hands of the service provider. The observations are
pithy and noteworthy and are as under:
The word compensation is of a very wide connotation. It may constitute
actual loss or expected loss and may extend to compensation for physical,
mental or even emotional suffering, insult or injury or loss. The provisions of
the
Consumer Protection Act
enable a consumer to claim and empower the
Commission to redress any injustice done. The Commission or the Forum is
entitled to award not only value of goods or services but also to compensate a
consumer for injustice suffered by him. The Commission/ Forum must determine
that such sufferance is due to malafide or capricious or oppressive act. It can
then determine amount for which the authority is liable to compensate the
consumer for his sufferance due to misfeasance in public office by the
officers. Such compensation is for vindicating the strength of law.
8. In
our view the District Forum has taken a very conservative view in awarding the compensation. We do not find any
infirmity in the impugned order and dismiss
the appeal.
9.
 F.D.R./ Bank Guarantee, if any,
furnished by the appellant be returned forthwith after completion of due
formalities.
10.
 A copy of this order as
per statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and
thereafter the file be consigned to the record room.
Announced on the 25th
 January, 2008.
(Justice J.D.
Kapoor)
